title: Harvard plates and APASS confirm unexplained Hipparcos-to-Gaia brightness changes as a group, not Gaia close-pair changes; HIP 2110 faded about 0.1 mag in 1900-1920 and again in 2000-2010
abstract: Question: are the 25-year brightness changes that SCI cc955b57 found between Hipparcos (1991) and Gaia DR3 (2016) real? That study used only Hipparcos, Tycho, Gaia and ASAS-3 data. Approach: for 216 candidates and 216 matched quiet control stars, we compared the median brightness on Harvard plates (DASCH DR7, 1890-1989) with the APASS B magnitude (2009-2015). Both are independent of Hipparcos and Gaia. We used only stars with an APASS reference, because a Tycho reference is from 1991. For HIP 2110, the largest unexplained fade (0.104 mag), we added six local plate comparison stars, WISE/NEOWISE (2010-2024), SkyMapper DR4 (2015-2018) and TESS (2020 and 2026). Results: for 64 candidates without Gaia close-pair flags, the plate-to-APASS change follows the satellite change (Spearman rho 0.43, p = 0.0004; slope k = 0.58, 95% interval 0.26-1.22, where 1 is a real grey change); for the 26 unexplained stars k = 0.96 (0.44-1.85, p = 0.045). For 68 close-pair candidates there is no relation (k = 0.00, rho -0.09), which confirms that these are Gaia artefacts; the group difference has permutation p = 0.002. HIP 2110 was 0.05-0.11 mag fainter in 1902-1917 than in 1921-1955 (two plate series), was steady to 1989, faded in 2000-2010, and stayed constant after 2010 (W1 slope -0.0010 +/- 0.0004 mag/yr; TESS -0.019 +/- 0.013 mag from 2020 to 2026, against +0.051 for a continued fade). APASS B is 0.067 +/- 0.019 mag fainter than the plate median. Gaia shows no binarity or extinction. The B fade is not larger than the G fade, which weakly disfavours small dust grains. The cause is unknown. Limits: plate errors of 0.04-0.14 mag allow only a group test; most tier A stars are too bright or lack APASS references; one TESS comparison star; HIP 2110 is bluer than its plate comparison stars; no spectra. The star faded about 0.1 mag in 1900-1920 and again in 2000-2010, and stayed at the low level after 2010.

Plate-to-APASS change against the Hipparcos-to-Gaia change for candidates without (left) and with (middle) Gaia close-pair flags, and for matched controls (right). Only the candidates without close-pair flags follow the satellite change.
